q: The cell membrane is also called the ______.
e: The cell membrane is also called the plasma membrane. Membranes are phospholipid bilayers that control transport and keep compartments. Tonoplast is not plasma membrane.

q: The plasma membrane is primarily made of a bilayer of ______.
e: The plasma membrane is primarily made of a bilayer of phospholipids. The plasma membrane is a phospholipid bilayer that controls what enters and leaves the cell. Carbohydrates is different: carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: In phospholipids, the phosphate head is ______.
e: In phospholipids, the phosphate head is hydrophilic. Hydrophilic heads face the watery surfaces of the membrane. Nonpolar is not hydrophilic.

q: The fatty acid tails of phospholipids are ______.
e: The fatty acid tails of phospholipids are hydrophobic. Hydrophobic tails hide from water in the membrane core. Hydrophilic is different: hydrophilic heads face the watery surfaces of the membrane.

q: Cholesterol in animal cell membranes helps to ______.
e: Cholesterol in animal cell membranes helps to maintain fluidity and stability. Cholesterol helps animal membranes stay fluid and stable. Increase permeability to ions is not maintain fluidity and stability.

q: Integral proteins may function as ______ in the membrane.
e: Integral proteins may function as channels or pumps in the membrane. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Waste products is not channels or pumps.

q: Carbohydrates on the cell surface are attached to proteins or lipids to form ______.
e: Carbohydrates on the cell surface are attached to proteins or lipids to form glycoproteins or glycolipids. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Nucleoproteins is not glycoproteins or glycolipids.

q: Carbohydrates on the cell membrane are important for ______.
e: Carbohydrates on the cell membrane are important for cell recognition. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Energy production is not cell recognition.

q: Passive transport does NOT require ______.
e: Passive transport does NOT require energy input. Living systems need a continual energy input to keep organised. A concentration gradient is not energy input.

q: Diffusion is the movement of molecules from ______.
e: Diffusion is the movement of molecules from high to low concentration. High to low concentration is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the membrane by ______.
e: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the membrane by simple diffusion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Facilitated diffusion is different: facilitated diffusion uses membrane proteins but still follows the gradient.

q: Facilitated diffusion uses ______ to transport substances.
e: Facilitated diffusion uses transport proteins to transport substances. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Facilitated diffusion uses membrane proteins but still follows the gradient. Endocytosis is not transport proteins.

q: Glucose enters red blood cells via ______.
e: Glucose enters red blood cells via facilitated diffusion. Facilitated diffusion uses membrane proteins but still follows the gradient. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range. Simple diffusion is not facilitated diffusion.

q: Osmosis is the net movement of ______ through a partially permeable membrane.
e: Osmosis is the net movement of water through a partially permeable membrane. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Osmosis is diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane. Ions is not water.

q: Water potential is higher in a ______ solution.
e: Water potential is higher in a dilute solution. Hypertonic is different: a hypertonic solution has higher solute and draws water out of cells.

q: In a hypertonic solution, an animal cell will ______.
e: In a hypertonic solution, an animal cell will shrink (crenate). A hypertonic solution has higher solute and draws water out of cells. Remain normal is not shrink (crenate).

q: In a hypotonic solution, a plant cell becomes ______.
e: In a hypotonic solution, a plant cell becomes turgid. A turgid cell is swollen with water and supports herbaceous shoots. A hypotonic solution has lower solute, so water enters the cell. Flaccid is not turgid.

q: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell is placed in a ______ solution.
e: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. A hypertonic solution has higher solute and draws water out of cells. Isotonic is different: an isotonic solution has the same water potential as the cell.

q: Active transport moves substances ______ the concentration gradient.
e: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. Down is different: an extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Active transport requires ______.
e: Active transport requires carrier proteins and ATP. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. Channel proteins is not carrier proteins and ATP.

q: Cyanide stops active transport by inhibiting ______.
e: Cyanide stops active transport by inhibiting ATP production. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. Membrane fluidity is not ATP production.

q: Phagocytosis is also known as ______.
e: Phagocytosis is also known as cell eating. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function. Cell drinking is not cell eating.

q: Pinocytosis is the uptake of ______.
e: Pinocytosis is the uptake of liquids and dissolved solutes. Solid particles is not liquids and dissolved solutes.

q: Exocytosis is used for ______.
e: Exocytosis is used for waste egestion and secretion. Nutrient uptake is not waste egestion and secretion.

q: Endocytosis and exocytosis involve the formation of ______.
e: Endocytosis and exocytosis involve the formation of vesicles. Ribosomes is different: ribosomes assemble proteins; they are not the site of photosynthesis.
